newsitem.title: CHINA: Southern China faces annual 25 mln T grain deficit.
newsitem.headline: Southern China faces annual 25 mln T grain deficit.

text.p: Huge swathes of southern China's coastal areas have faced grain shortages in recent years, with the annual supply deficit totalling around 25 million tonnes, Shanghai's Business News said on Wednesday.
Southern China used to be one of China's major grain-producing areas, supplying rice and other staples to the north, the newspaper said.
But output in the region has failed to keep pace with overall increases in grain production, it said.
Between 1983 and 1995, when China's grain output increased by 79.34 million tonnes, northern China's output rose 70 percent but production in southern China only rose 30 percent, it said.
By 1994, 10 of the 15 provinces in southern China faced grain shortages totalling around 25 million tonnes a year, the newspaper said.
As a result, every year grain must be shipped from the north to the south to maintain a balance in supply, it said.
China's 1996 grain harvest was a record 480 million tonnes. A total of about six million tonnes of corn has been shipped from northern growing regions to needy areas in south in the past few months.
